title: FOMO marketing: bet on what's working, explore with 20%
summary: Cody defines FOMO marketing as deciding based on what you could be doing instead of what is working. He frames marketing as a portfolio (80% on proven channels, 20% on exploration) and says to keep scaling a winning channel until returns diminish, using a 13x ROAS Google Search example.

principles.text: FOMO marketing means choosing based on what you could do, not on what is working.
principles.quote: FOMO marketing is when we make marketing decisions based on what we could be doing rather than what is working.

principles.text: Treat marketing as a portfolio: 80% on proven channels, 20% on exploring new ones.
principles.quote: I think about marketing as a portfolio, where 80% of resources is spent on what is working and 20% on an exploration of new initiatives.

principles.text: Scale a winning channel until diminishing returns show up before expanding elsewhere.
principles.quote: I told him literally put as much money into that channel until you see diminishing returns. Go to that ATM until it quits printing.

principles.text: Shiny object syndrome distracts marketing teams from their purpose: increasing revenue.
principles.quote: A lot of marketing teams get shiny object syndrome and which distracts them from why they exist: to increase revenue.

principles.text: Keep testing new things, but with only a small share of resources.
principles.quote: And I'm not saying don't test new things. But allocated a small percentage of resources.

principles.text: Make bets for both the short term and the long term.
principles.quote: We're making bets for the short term, and bets for the long term.
